newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says island dispute with UAE belongs to past.
newsitem.headline: Iran says island dispute with UAE belongs to past.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Sunday dismissed the issue of three Gulf islands disputed by the United Arab Emirates as belonging to the past.
But he said Tehran was ready to hold talks with the UAE to clear up any misunderstandings.
"This goes back to 1971 when Iran had some claims over Bahrain and the British were the power bullying in the region and they created these differences," Rafsanjani told a Tehran news conference.
Britain withdrew its military protection from the Arab side of the Gulf in December 1971, giving rise to the creation of the UAE and other Gulf Arab states.

Tehran and Abu Dhabi dispute ownership of the islands of Abu Musa and Greater and Lesser Tunbs, now held by Iran. Gulf Arab states have long demanded an end to Iranian "occupation" of the islands located near oil tanker routes at the entrance to the Gulf.
"We do not find it expedient to have a revival of problems which existed before the (1979) revolution," Rafsanjani said.
"But we are ready to have negotiations and whenever they (the UAE) are ready we could continue doing so."
Rafsanjani said "some prejudices and instigations by the United States and Britain served as an impediment to solving the problem".
